newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's unemployment falls to 9.7 pct in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Canada's unemployment falls to 9.7 pct in Dec.

text.p: Statistics Canada said on Friday the unemployment rate fell to 9.7 percent in December from 10.0 percent in November.
Note - Labor force, employment and unemployment in millions, on seasonally adjusted basis.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the unemployment rate to drop to 9.84 percent and employment to grow by 30,500 in November.

Statistics Canada said the overall drop in the unemployment rate was due to a combination of increased employment among adults and a decline in the number of young people (aged 15 to 24) in the labor force.

Job gains among adults totalled 209,000 in 1996, as women gained 110,000 jobs and men gained 99,000 jobs. Almost all gains for adult men were in full-time employment, while most women's jobs were part-time.
In 1996, employment grew at twice the pace of the previous year, but below the 2.9 percent increase of 1994, Statistics Canada said.
The employment rate edged down 0.1 percent in 1996 to 58.5 percent as the rate of employment failed to keep up with population growth.

Employment among young people fell 20,000 in the year, leaving their employment rate 0.7 percentage points down at 51.1 percent. The unemployment rate for young people stood at 16.4 percent at the end of the year.
In December, 27,000 jobs were created in community, business and personal services and 8,000 new jobs were created in the other primary industries.
Public administration lost 12,000 jobs and agriculture lost 8,000.
